profile.name: SeongGyeong Park
profile.role: Ph.D. Candidate · The University of Texas at Austin
profile.tagline: I study how immigrant families navigate schools—and how educational institutions can build more equitable partnerships.
profile.summary: My work connects newcomer parental engagement, social capital, and educational leadership across schools and communities.
profile.bio:
I am a Ph.D. candidate in Education Policy and Planning at The University of Texas at Austin. My scholarship examines educational equity through the experiences and knowledge of immigrant families.

I draw on community-engaged research and asset-based perspectives to explore how families participate in education—and how schools can respond more equitably.

research.title: Immigrant Family Engagement
research.description: Newcomer parents’ experiences, agency, and relationships with schools.

research.title: Social Capital & Equity
research.description: Networks, resources, and institutional conditions shaping educational opportunity.

research.title: School–Community Partnerships
research.description: How leaders and community organizations support meaningful family engagement.

dissertation.title: Understanding Newcomer Immigrant Parental Engagement within U.S. Schools
dissertation.description: A qualitative case study exploring newcomer parents’ engagement experiences, the role of social capital, and how educational institutions support or constrain engagement. The study centers families’ perspectives and attends to relationships among schools, families, and community organizations.
